newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ukraine deputy PM says country taming inflation.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine deputy PM says country taming inflation.

text.p: Ukrainian deputy prime minister Victor Pynzenyk said on Friday that the country was taming inflation and that it should hit around 10 percent by the end of the century from previous runaway levels.
He said the country expected inflation of 25 percent from December 1996 to December 1997 compared with 40 percent in 1996.
He made the comments at a news conference where the World Bank announced that multilateral organisations and donor countries undertook on Friday to plug Ukraine's $1.8 billion financing gap for 1997.

The World Bank and International Monetary fund pledged a provisional $1.4 billion, while the United States, Japan and the European Union were expected to contribute a total of some $400 million. The contributions are to be confirmed at a pledging session in Washington next month.

Pynzenyk said the country should show two percent real gross domestic product growth in 1997 for the first time since its independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991. Growth is expected to rise to four to six percent in later years.
Ukraine launched a major economic reform programme in 1994.
The country's central bank governor Viktor Yuschenko noted that Ukraine had enjoyed a stable currency for 15 months with a fluctation rate of around 1.2 percent.

The 15 donor nations and eight multinational organisations at the meeting praised Ukraine for pressing ahead with structural reforms agreed with the World Bank and for meeting fiscal and monetary targets set with the International Monetary Fund.
They said that 1997 "could be a definitive turning point" for the Ukrainian economy.
The group noted, however, that the economic outlook would hinge on maintaining political consensus on the reforms.
